description: TisDass - rock touareg from Niger TisDass, hailing from Niger, is set for another European tour in 2026. Following the military putsch in August 2023, which led to the cancellation of a significant portion of their tour, the band successfully returned to European stages in 2025 with 32 dates across 9 countries. Tisdass is led by singer-guitarist Moussa Kildjate Albadé, and is based in Niamey with roots in Tchintabaraden, a town emblematic of the Tamasheq kel of Niger. "TisDass" means 'Pillars' in Tamasheq, a reference to the pillars of traditional Berber tents. This name signifies the group's deep connection to their culture, which they aim to defend and promote through their powerful music. Houmaïssa, released by Bolingo Art/Rebel Up (Inouïe Distribution), is named after a Tuareg symbol exclusively worn by women. With this album, TisDass pays homage to women, who are considered the pillars of the family in Tuareg society. While the album features a quicker tempo, the acoustic tracks "Tara" (Love) and "Itag Aguen" (Many things are happening) maintain the distinctive sound of Sahelian music. The remaining tracks showcase the rock direction the band has embraced on stage. The songs' themes consistently reflect the Tuareg people's desire and hope for peace, as heard in "Taflist" (Trust), "Derhan" (Hope), and "Ikewagne" (Root). The inspiration for a third album arose when the current line-up toured to support Amanar (Bolingo Art), recorded in 2019 and released in 2021 (Inouïe Distribution). Since then, TisDass' music has evolved into a decidedly rock sound with more danceable tracks, thanks to the contributions of rhythm guitarist Mouhamed Khamed Assalerh, the faster drumming of young Issoufou Dan Nana Ichaya, and the enhanced groove from experienced bassist Bouba Hamidine Souleymane. The ever-present backing vocals and claps further enrich their sound. description: Parkhof night at OCCII:: a film, a book, a band film: Is er meer dan de straat (20 min.) book: De slag om Parkhof (160 pag.) band: Wanda's (dr gtr gtr bs v) Parkhof was a famous, infamous squat venue annex youth-center in the city of Alkmaar. Since the late 70s, for more than 25 years, it was the place to be for kids of all ages and backgrounds, fans of DIY culture and punk music. Like an OCCII avant-la-lettre. And yes, we know, Parkhof has ceased to be, a sign of the times alas, but the ideas and ideals are still alive. Coincidence or not, but all of a sudden snippets from a punky underground past find their way to the surface and are out in the open again. So yeah, here's a helluva tripple bill for ya not like any other. Like, the viewing of the short experimental lowbudget? nobudget! movie "Is er meer dan de straat" (Is there more than the street), made on a shoestring by four young students in 1981, a visual final-year thesis about DIY and/in Parkhof... a movie that recently, after 45 years, attracted the attention of the renowned Rijksmuseum, to become part of its collection. Like, the book launch of the new book "De slag om Parkhof" (The battle of Parkhof) by Marleen Kamminga en Bamber Delver, which tells the his&herstory of this music space that was so much more than just a place to hang out. Interviews with the people who lived there, who worked there, who played there, who visited concerts there, plus photo's and posters. And a plea for more free space where the youngsters of now can be/become who they want to be. Like, the concert by the recently resurrected feminist punk/rock band the Wanda's, who were part of the Parkhof story from the very beginning, they actually ran the place, one might say. The band lasted about ten years, did a lot of gigs nationwide, made two albums, disappeared into oblivion, and since a year or so they're back... Angry Old Women, ready to set your hearing (aids) to the test, 'cause Punk is stil Not Deaf. Come and join us, it'll be fun. # # # IS THERE MORE THAN THE STREET Four young, eager students at the social academy, in their final year, time for their graduation thesis, and not in the mood for it. Not for a stack of paper full of text that would end up in a filing cabinet that no one would ever look into again. What they DID want: to tell something about the do-it-yourself punk culture that was raging around them right there in 1980, '81. Showing something about that, about how you can shape your own future yourself, well now, THAT did appeal to them. In short, they decided to make a film. They had no clue, really, never done it before, but they did it anyway. Themselves. Anyway, they just started, with borrowed equipment, and they stuck the theme "Do It Yourself" to the squatted youth center Parkhof in Alkmaar, where a group of female punks in particular ran the place. Plus something about making fanzines and releasing your own records. Through trial and error they discovered what worked and what didn't, resulting in a film of no less than 20 minutes, on Super 8. The result was to be expected: primitive and (somewhat unintentionally) experimental, but also sincere and full of passion. And 45 years later, that little piece of captured 80s zeitgeist has turned out to be as urgent as fuck once again, having actually never really gone away. WANDA'S Wanda's plays classic punk in a contemporary form. Even more urgent than they did in the 1980s, because the time is more than ripe for a major punk revival. In the late 70s, six girlfriends, all active in the squatted punk venue Parkhof, decided to start a band together. An adventure that would last nine years, countless gigs, several line-up changes, and two LPs. Over the years, their sound transformed from experimental rattle punk to solid punk rock with a (feminist) message. About 35 years later, they looked each other up again, and the musical and personal connection had remained unchanged. And so, ever since, they have happily continued working on their hearing damage: Punks Not Deaf! From noisy teenagers to Angry Old Women, Wanda's keep on keeping on rocking hard. https://wandas.bandcamp.com/ wandas.nl THE BATTLE OF PARKHOF A squatted school that grew into one of the most famous punk venues in the Netherlands. That is the story of Parkhof, the Alkmaar haven where generations of young people shaped their own culture between 1980 and 2009. In the new book "The Battle for Parkhof – How Punk Conquered Alkmaar" Marleen Kamminga and Bamber Delver bring this remarkable history back to life. Through dozens of personal stories, original photos, and posters, the authors tell how Parkhof grew into the beating heart of the regional punk scene. At a time when large music venues hardly existed, young people built their own stage and created a sanctuary where music, creativity, and the punk motto Do It Yourself took center stage. Kamminga and Delver, former Parkhof punks themselves, spoke with former visitors, residents, musicians, and youth workers. Together, their memories form a vivid picture of a place that was much more than a youth center for thousands of young people. At the same time, the book shows how themes such as housing shortages, identity, solidarity, and the search for a place of one's own remain relevant today. According to the authors, the book is therefore not only a look back at a special period in Alkmaar's history but also a plea for sanctuaries where young people can be themselves and develop their own culture. With "The Battle for Parkhof," a unique chapter from recent history receives the recognition it deserves.
title: PARKHOF NIGHT w/ WANDA'S + THE BATTLE OF PARKHOF (BOOK) + IS THERE MORE THAN THE STREET (FILM) + GW SOK (q/a)

description: DEAD MIND RECORDS & CHARNEL GROUND PRESENT: Kazumoto Endo (JP) + Violent Shogun (FR) + Corpse Magnetism (CZ/NL) + Musica Divina (FI/BE) + Awenydd Day 2 of the Dead Mind Festival, continuing the festival’s focus on experimental sound, noise and underground collaboration. The evening includes a second performance by noise legend Kazumoto Endo and two unique collaborative projects. Day one of the Dead Mind Festival will be held Saturday 10th of October at the Willem Twee Toonzaal, The Bosch with performances by Rudolf Eb.er, Wanderwelle, Kazomoto Endo, BJ Nilsen, The Haters, Orphan Fairytale, Haare, Beequeen, Ernst Bonis & Asch. Kazumoto Endo is a Japanese noise musician known for his intense, dynamic approach to harsh noise and electronic sound manipulation. Emerging in the mid-90s under the legendary Killer Bug moniker, he quickly became part of the Japanese noise elite. Endo is best known for highly compressed, rapidly shifting sonic assaults built from distortion, feedback and fragmented electronic signals, often delivered with abrupt structural changes and a raw, improvisational feel. He started releasing records under his own name in 1997 and the 1999 While You Were Out album stands as a perfectly crafted modern classic of Japanese harsh noise, helping establish his reputation internationally within the extreme music community. Violent Shogun is a French experimental noise musician known for dense, abrasive soundscapes that blend industrial textures, tape manipulation, broken sounds and musique concrète. Emerging from the underground noise scene in the late 2010s, the project has released a series of limited albums through various independent labels like Satatuhatta. These releases explore themes like decay, isolation, violence and social collapse through restrained sonic intensity. Violent Shogun collaborated with underground noise artists like HÖH from Finland and is known for a unique approach to sound art. Corpse Magnetism is a collaborative project between Rudolf Eb.er (Switzerland, currently residing in Japan) and Johnny van de Koolwijk (Netherlands). Rooted in ritualistic sound practices and primitive outsider aesthetics, the duo creates immersive sonic environments built from organic drones, handmade instruments, decayed textures, primitive percussion and improvised field recordings. Rudolf Eb.er aka Runzelstirn & Gurgelstøck is widely known for founding the radical outsider art project Schimpfluch-Gruppe in 1987, as well as being involved in numerous projects over the last few decades, exploring trance states, body art and shamanistic expression. He has worked together with noise legends like Masonna, Joke Lanz and for this occasion will perform with Van de Koolwijk, who has been active in the Dutch experimental underground under the alias ZRTX, focusing on raw ambient structures, lo-fi tape loops and sound collages. Musica Divina is a collaborative noise and sound art project formed by Haare (Finland) and Vincent Dalles (Belgium). Rooted in long-form improvisation and environmental texture, the duo creates immersive sonic landscapes built from dense organic drones, metal scraping and concrete sound manipulation. Drawing inspiration from the organic minimalism and material-focused approach of artists like Jeph Jerman, Musica Divina explores the physicality of sound through slow-moving, tactile compositions that blur the boundaries between noise, industrial ambience and electro-acoustic experimentation. With an LP coming out on Dead Mind and Bent Window we are honoured to welcome them for a first ever live performance. Awenydd initially operated as a private, studio-based outlet for raw sound experiments, but the project gradually developed into a more defined artistic identity through a small series of self-released, limited cassette editions, circulating within the noise network. Drawing from dark ambient and various noise traditions, Awenydd creates tightly controlled, immersive compositions built from layered drones, metallic resonance and shifting sonic textures. Inspired by the physical properties of sound, Awenydd’s work balances harsh textures, introspective atmospheres, subconscious landscapes and shifting states of mind. The project gained attention for its consistency of vision a commitment to raw, unmediated sound practice.
title: Kazumoto Endo (JP) + Violent Shogun (FR) + Corpse Magnetism (CZ/NL) + Musica Divina (FI/BE) + Awenydd

description: A night of Total Music #2:: FRED FRITH, TIM HODGKINSON & LIZ ALBEE (US/UK/DE) + LUKRAAK (Marcus Wärnheim & Thomas Jaspers) + JOSHUA BURKETT (US) - a dazzling celebration of the unexpected – contemplative and ecstatic, unruly and gloriously alive - FRED FRITH + TIM HODGKINSON + LIZ ALBEE (US/UK/DE) A meeting of three outstanding improvisational musicians who understand sound as an open territory. Guitar legend Fred Frith – co-founder of Henry Cow and a defining figure in experimental music since the 1970s – encounters Tim Hodgkinson, a comrade from those radical early days and an tireless explorer of improvisation, composition, and sound anthropology. Joining them is Liz Allbee, a Berlin-based trumpeter and sound artist who transforms her instrument into a vibrating resonant body of breath, electronics, and material experimentation. A fully improvised trialogue – raw, poetic, and unpredictable. The combination of Frith's prepared guitar/string work, Hodgkinson's intense reed work/composition, and Albee's trumpet/electronics represents a high-level intersection of veteran avant-garde and experimental improvisation. Multi-instrumentalist, composer, and improviser Fred Frith has been making noise of one kind or another for more than 50 years, starting with the rock collective Henry Cow, which he co-founded with Tim Hodgkinson in 1968. Fred is best known as a pioneering electric guitarist and improviser, song-writer, and composer for film, dance and theater. Through bands like Art Bears, Massacre, Skeleton Crew, the Fred Frith Guitar Quartet, Cosa Brava, and now Fremakajo he has stayed close to his roots in rock and folk music while branching out in many other directions. Fred has performed works by and sometimes alongside composers Alvin Curran, Meredith Monk, Pauline Oliveros, Terry Riley, and Christian Wolff; improvised with Lotte Anker, Derek Bailey, Han Bennink, Peter Brötzmann, Lol Coxhill, Janet Feder, gabby fluke-mogul, Tim Hodgkinson, Joëlle Léandre, Phil Minton, Ikue Mori, Butch Morris, Bob Ostertag, Evan Parker, Zeena Parkins, Paula Sanchez, Susana Santos Silva and Camel Zekri, to name a few; and—as session musician—recorded on albums by, for example, Brian Eno, The Residents, Robert Wyatt, The Swans, Violent Femmes, Material, Negativland, John Zorn, Matthew and the Unfortunates, and Half Japanese. https://www.fredfrith.com/live/ Tim Hodgkinson (b. 1949) studied social anthropology at Cambridge, and co-founded the politically and musically radical group HENRY COW with Fred Frith in 1968. In addition to composing, he has a long involvement in improvisation, and came back to anthropology in the 1990's with research into music and shamanism in Siberia. As an improvising musician on reeds and lap steel guitar Tim Hodgkinson has performed all over the world with many of the most acclaimed artists in the field, and continues to be fully engaged in the celebrated Konk Pack trio with Roger Turner and Thomas Lehn. In 2009 he released KLARNT - a CD of solo clarinet improvisations. http://www.timhodgkinson.co.uk/ Liz Allbee is a trumpet player who doesn’t play the trumpet all that often. Or at least, not the regular one. Instead, she frequently opts for a quadrophonic trumpet of her own design, as well as her voice and a myriad of self-made objects. The case in point is her recent album Breath Vessels, made using various glasses, pots and dismantled second-hand instruments which produce a surprisingly melodious drone. Often radical, Allbee is also an economic composer and improviser: prudent layering of loops provides a smooth passage towards trance. An uneasy one – since Allbee’s inspiration comes from recent events like the sinking of the ship Adriana with hundreds of migrants on board in 2023, or from a withering observation the problems of our planet started when humans evolved opposable thumbs. A consoling one – since her work is conceived as new folk music, driven not by nostalgia but by a sense of community. https://lizallbee.net/ LUKRAAK Lukraak plays post-silly music of crooked beauty. Using alto saxophone, drums, flutes, found objects as well as their own centered bodies and flying limbs, they produce something of their own with a haphazard attitude. Intricate sonic mosaics and vivid tapestries of complex sound masses are created along the edges of experimental jazz and neo-neo-dada-dada. Lukraak has previously performed at Porta-Jazz Festival and Valkhof Festival, as well as at venues in the Netherlands, Germany, Sweden, Denmark, Belgium, France, Poland and the Baltics. They are individually and collectively active members of the vibrant experimental music scene of Amsterdam, and together with Jaap Blonk they perform as Luk&BlonkRaak. On 26th of September 2025 their debut album 'Zaalig' was released on LukRecords. Marcus Wärnheim - alto saxophone, recorders and other stuff Thomas Jaspers - drums, cymbals, recorders and other stuff https://lukraak.bandcamp.com/album/zaalig https://youtu.be/48Aj7v-mEXA?si=_c9Qqe0iB_4R0Lj3 JOSHUA BURKETT (US) Joshua Burkett is a musician, writer, illustrator, painter, & naturalist and has been a guiding light of the Western Massachusetts underground music community for the past 30 years. After leaving CT & Boston came Josh's debut album ("OwlLeavesRustling" which he self released in 1995) which is one the first examples of what would much later come to be known as "Free Folk", "Freak Folk", &/or "New Weird America". He has many other lps and duo collaborations under his belt since then, including 'Gold Cosmos' and 'Where's My Hat' plus 'Footnote(s)' and 'Yellowbeard' on the Ultra Eczema label. He also worked with the late, great Ed Askew, releasing a duo album with the phenomenal Tucker Zimmerman in 2020, his electronic project TARP with Conrad Capistran, plus his recent duo project with the amazing Lau Nau and others. Burkett is doing a few special shows this year to celebrate his new lp 'M/B/Too/4/T/&/M' (out soon on the Futura Resistenza label!) https://www.cafeoto.co.uk/artists/joshua-burkett/

description: Saba Alizadeh Architect of Power Ambient Saba Alizadeh occupies a singular space in contemporary music ,a sonic language so distinct it seems to exist outside comparison. Coming from a distinguished musical lineage and shaped by more than two decades as a composer, producer, and performer, he has developed an artistic voice that merges deep cultural memory with fearless sonic experimentation. Across four critically acclaimed albums, he has continuously expanded the boundaries between contemporary composition, electronic music, and Persian sonic heritage. Having lived through defining social and political ruptures - from witnessing the fall of the Berlin Wall as a child to experiencing the Green Movement and the Woman, Life, Freedom uprising in Iran - his work carries the emotional residue of history not as commentary, but as lived memory transformed into sound. Emerging from Tehran’s underground electronic scene, Alizadeh forged a deeply personal language where Persian classical music, experimental electronics, archival recordings, and cinematic tension dissolve into what critics have called “Power Ambient.” At the center of his performances stands the Kamancheh: the ancient Persian bowed instrument whose raw, human cry he reshapes through live processing and sonic experimentation into something both ancestral and radically contemporary. His live sets unfold like fragments of forgotten cinema - dense, haunting, and physical. Continuously reimagining how history, memory, and resistance can breathe through modern sound. ''A bridge between the ancient and the contemporary'' — The Wire ''A fresh, compelling soundscape'' — Pitchfork ''Hope as an act of resistance'' — Frankfurter Rundschau ''Music that feels like a cinematic unfolding of history'' — Chain D.L.K. ''The stringed Kamancheh is a living soul and primal voice'' — Veil of Sound Temple Of Hope by Saba Alizadeh INSTAGRAM Farzané (Farzaneh Nouri), an Iranian sound artist, creative coder, and researcher based in the Netherlands, works at the intersection of experimental music and computer science. Her ongoing practice-based research focuses on embodied knowledge in improvisational settings with machines. Embracing AI's fundamental otherness while establishing relational connections, her practice aims at creating conditions of genuine encounter and collaborative destabilization between the artist and the machine. This speculative approach moves beyond technological determinism and cultural essentialism, exploring how human and machine intelligences might co-evolve through creative tension and collaborative aesthetic discovery. INSTAGRAM CHIASMA by Farzané VEHICLE/PASSENGER Ethereal yet full of raw power. A tour-de-force of artistic expression combined with an urgent message on the state of our world. In VEHICLE/PASSENGER we gather around thoughtful, radical poetry, as it weaves through energetically improvised pieces and delicate soundscapes. Exploring a queer perspective on body, society and improvisation. The trio reveals a unified, futuristic sound, repositioning the past, present and future of experimental music, free jazz, hip-hop, live electronics and poetry. "An energy and urgency without simple slogans." - WDR, Odilo Clausnitzer "Vehicle/Passenger has created one of the most honest and unique recordings of 2024." - All About Jazz, Maurice Hoge M Alberto (NL/AN) - poetry , saxophones and electronics Lesley Mok (US) - drums and percussion Florian Herzog (DE) - double bass and electronics M. ALBERTO (they/them), is a Euro-Carribean improviser, award-winning poet and composer. Born in Curacao and currently based in the Netherlands. M.’s work is explicitly political, and always critical of colonial structures. They are one of the driving forces behind theatre collectives Boys won’t be Boys, as well as a steady collaborator in other critical productions. They have performed internationally on diverse stages and theatres from The Royal Concertgebouw and the Dutch National Opera to pop-festivalslike Sziget, Rock Werchter and Pinkpop. FLORIAN HERZOG, bassist and composer, is a pioneer of the German and international jazz and avant-garde scenes whose bass playing has been described by the press as "emancipated, spirited and sensitive." He has worked with established greats like Theo Bleckmann, Jim Black and Nils Wogram, but also with the new generation and musicians like Anna Webber, Elias Stemeseder and Nick Dunston. LESLEY MOK (they/them) is a percussionist and interdisciplinary artist based in Brooklyn, NY, who works in sound, installation, film, and theater. Interested in the ways social conditions shape our beings, Lesley’s work focuses on overacting humanness to explore ideas about alienness and privilege. Their work draws from queer and feminist art practices, Chinese philosophy, Caribbean folkloric musical traditions, futurist perspectives, and ancestral knowledge. Their critically acclaimed debut album ‘The Living Collection’ was awarded with a prestigious Deutscher Jazz Preis in 2024. INSTAGRAM

description: Pretty//Ugly presents a night of queer folk radical traditionals Goblin Band https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Bt-laPpfJek "They can play and they can sing and they’re fearless...” "The band we've been waiting for" - MARTIN CARTHY “One of the most magnificent things this listener has heard in a long, long time.” -MOOF Mag “They throw down challenges, invite questions, and warm hearts.” -Sidmouth Herald Goblin Band are a four-piece English traditional folk band based in London. The band formed in the wake of the pandemic from small sessions organised by young, queer, folk obsessive friends looking to forge their own way into traditional music. This gave rise to a band of multi-instrumentalists firmly rooted in the music of England, concerned with representing a perspective that confronts the nation’s social and political history of class struggle, industrialisation and colonialism. Through a fusion of harmony singing, fiddle, squeezeboxes, hurdy gurdy and more, Goblin Band deliver a charismatic and unruly alternative expression of English traditional music both riotously joyful and deeply sincere. Come Slack Your Horse! by Goblin Band The Silver Field The Silver Field is a sound world of Coral Rose Kindred-Boothby. Voice, tapes, bass, samples, synthesis, strings, reeds, drums, small sounds, big sounds, sunlight, moonlight, a lot of water. Using her modular synthesiser and other self-built electronic instruments, she weaves together song-soundscapes, creating a rich and dream-like tapestry of sound that draws from folk music tradition, experimental electronics and psychedelia. Her LPs 'Rooms' and 'Sing High! Sing Low', and split EP with Betwixt & Between Tapes received press in The Guardian, Mojo and The Quietus among others, and have had radio play and guest playlists on BBC 6Music and NTS. On Sing High! Sing Low! you can actually hear that slow and organic growth, its layers that reveal themselves all at once, creating a psychedelic drift through time and space. It’s a record of juxtapositions, between sung and spoken vocals, acoustic and electric instrumentation. Its images and environments feel evocative and real, but also imbued with a universal sense of essence. description: An evening full of raw American Primitive fingerpicking Double bill: Glenn Jones & Liam Grant + 1 More TBA Glenn Jones is a master of American Primitive Guitar, a style invented in the late 1950s by John Fahey. Jones, who led the post-rock ensemble Cul de Sac, brings his own made-up tunings, the use of custom-crafted partial capos, and a highly skilled picking style on both banjo and guitar, to create personal compositions that are lyrical, emotive and elegant. https://glennjones.bandcamp.com/music Liam Grant (Boston, MA) is a New England guitarist with a punk ethos, cut from the American Primitive cloth. The restless guitar explorations, modal epics and driving uptempo rags recall the likes of Grant's pedagogue: Takoma Records and the path that was paved by his forebears John Fahey, Robbie Basho, Peter Walker, Max Ochs and later Glenn Jones, Steffen Basho-Junghans, Jack Rose, and others. https://liamgrant.bandcamp.com Glenn Jones first made a name for himself with the ‘rock band’ Cul De Sac, a band that played with Can-singer Damo Suzuki more often than Can itself. Since then, he has become one of the most important American Primitive guitarists of the 21st century. Over the course of ten albums, Jones has developed an undeniably unique fingerstyle voice. His music forms a deeply personal melodic grammar: witty, reflective and rooted in memory. Sketches of Fahey, his friendship with John Jackson, early visits to 78 rpm collector Joe Bussard and his bond with Jack Rose all leave their mark on his work. Equally present are the tender portraits of his mother, Nora Smith, and the small anchor points in daily life, such as his beloved cats. Jones’ compositions feel like living memories, shaped by curiosity, dedication and the fleeting beauty of everyday life. Over the years, he has remained a vital figure in the underground scene, someone who continually refines and reinvents the steel-string tradition. His pieces carry emotional power without sentimentality and are anchored in experience, yet always open to surprise. Liam Grant draws deeply from the landscape in which he grew up: memoires of the Merrimack, Amoskeag and the waters flowing toward the great flood of Dead River. He has toured extensively in the US and beyond since 2021 and regularly works with Glenn Jones and fiddler Mike Gangloff. His debut album Amoskeag (2023) confirmed his place as a rising voice within the steel-string tradition. His album Prodigal Son (2025, VHF Records) – a lo-fi statement for 12 string, 6 string and lap steel guitar – was praised by NPR’s Viking’s Choice and featured among The Quietus’ and Wilco’s favourite albums of 2025. Grant’s collaborations include releases with Gangloff, Sam Shalabi and members of The Three-Top Serenaders, as well as contributions to compilations like The Sun Is Not True. He is among the young players revitalising the American Primitive vocabulary, still rooted in tradition but driven by curiosity and shaped by the rivers and history of New England. 12V5 - mechanic movements and self constructed instruments (FRance). Sonic shadows and sounds from 12V bulbs and motors, a casio synthesiser, wooden and metallic objects. Feedbacks and trumpets. Improvising with scanners and photocopy machines. Neon tubes directly plugged into the mixer making random rhythms. Dance to the sound of a sonic scrap yard. description: LE GUESS WHO? & U? PRESENT: TOTALLY WIRED in collaboration with ANTIPODE, OCCII, GIRLS TO THE FRONT and ZALZALA DIY LIVE MUSIC FESTIVAL, ZINE LAUNCH, SCREENING, EXHIBITION, MARKET & WORKSHOPS This year, Le Guess Who? and U? are teaming up to present totally wired. Built on shared knowledge and collective energy, this program celebrates DIY culture, the communities that shape it, and the connections forged across borders through local scenes, diasporas and intersections. The program features a collective zine launch, workshop, exhibition, screenings, market of local artists and distros, and a line-up connecting different shades of punk and bringing exciting and loud voices together. totally wired takes place on Saturday, 7 November, at dB's in Utrecht and is freely accessible. totally wired is curated in collaboration with Antipode, a project that documents underground punk and DIY culture from SWANA and beyond; Girls to the Front, an Utrecht based initiative focused on the Dutch based FLINTA representation within the punk music industry; OCCII, an independent cultural center in Amsterdam that celebrates underground music; and ZALZALA, a DIY collective that celebrates underground hardcore and punk music from SWANA. >>> https://leguesswho.com/news/totally-wired The lineup includes BeaBop, an Amsterdam based project that brings together ideas from noise, jazz, punk, improvisation, dissociation, hunger and whimsy; four-piece terror squad BOMBSTRAP, hailing from Manchester and Rotterdam, bringing nihilistic hardcore rooted in black alchemy and ultra violence; Gimic—a four-piece band who live and breath DIY punk—which is urgent, restless and dynamic; rapper, producer and multi-instrumentalist Emirhan X, who constantly explores and pushes the boundaries of hip-hop; Bristol based underground hardcore band Sarsour صرصور—the Arabic word for cockroach—delivering raw, politically charged music self-described as "Habibi Hardcore"; Snake Eater مارخور, with the sound of the screw horns of war against colonialism worldwide, blending hardcore punk, grind core and metal into an unrelenting sonic maelstrom; five-piece band Sublux, driven by the marginalized identities and where they intersect; all-female conceptual punk band The Earwurms, who explore how being women affects their lives and how to deal with the confusion that comes along with it; The Woman, who, with a distinct mix of alternative and experimental music, gritty poetry and visual art, creates an immersive performance that is punk in attitude, open in emotion and radical in honesty; and Berlin based ZANJEER زنجیر, who set audiences ablaze with their blistering hardcore assault, through which they give voice to the frustration, anger and hatred stemming from systematic and ongoing oppression. dB's oefenstudio's, concertzaal & muziekcafé Vlampijpstraat 63 3534 AR Utrecht https://dbstudio.nl/(opens in new tab) Snake Eater مارخور With grindy, metal-tinged hardcore riffs, a broken-up buzzsaw guitar tone from gear that survived a house fire, relentless d-beat and raw punk energy, Snake Eater مارخور delivers furious, abrasive sounds. Inspired by Pakistani-Punjabi poetry and musical traditions, their lyrics channel an uncompromising anti-imperialist message. Fierce and confrontational, Snake Eater is the sound of the screws horns of war against colonialism worldwide, blending hardcore punk, grind core and metal into an unrelenting sonic maelstrom. Gimic Urgent, restless and dynamic, Gimic's music twists and turns at every corner, resembling a band of four people who live and breathe DIY Punk. The rhythm section is locked in and in perfect harmony whilst the guitar tone is clean and sharp, but it’s the blood-curdling vocals that give it that confrontational and emotional edge. Imagine Minutemen's hardcore era mixed with the angular precision of math rock and the impeccable musicianship of No Means No. BOMBSTRAP "For fans of No Trend, Total Abuse and dead healthcare CEO’s”, four piece terror squad BOMBSTRAP plays nihilistic hardcore rooted in black alchemy and ultraviolence. Born in the anarchistic community of Poortgebouw in Rotterdam, over the past couple of years they unleashed a tidal wave of shows through DIY stages in the Netherlands and beyond. Their debut album Big Enemy is a sonic bullet: caustic, explosive hardcore drowned in nihilism and charged with anarchic alchemy aimed straight at the heart of a corrupt society. The Woman With a distinct mix of alternative and experimental music, gritty poetry and visual art, The Woman creates an immersive performance that is punk in attitude, open in emotion and radical in honesty. Led by Sheyda Abolfath, the project tells the melodramatic story of the modern man in search of a soul, while portraying the world as an ugly, dirty and elusive place where beauty can be found for those who listen. BeaBop Emerging from Amsterdam thriving improvised music scene, BeaBop is a new quartet where noise, jazz, punk, improvisation, dissociation, hunger and whimsy collide in exhilarating ways. Bringing together four adventurous musicians for the local-international scene - vocalist Beatrice Sberna, bassist Omer Brandt, guitarist Tina Czernik and drummer Aviv Maya - the project is rooted in a community of artists constantly crossing paths through a wide range of bands and collaborations. Emirhan X Known for his energetic live performances and distinctive sound, Emirhan X combines raw rap with influences from punk, boom bap and a touch of experimental music. His lyrics balance confident bravado, disarming vulnerability and politically charged messages that challenge himself and his listeners to face real emotions. With his unique vocal sound, the rapper and producer effortlessly switches between powerful raps and compelling vocal lines, making his music both intense and accessible. Sublux A hardcore punk band with a spooky anarcho twist, Sublux move between unhinged speed, ominous doom and heavy emotional depth with big riffs, chaotic synths, a pummelling rhythm section and piercing banshee vocals. Their line-up is primarily women, primarily Asian and two-thirds wheelchair users; the band's name itself refers to a symptom of their shared disability. Their lyrics explore grief and rage towards a societal history of selfishness and cruelty whilst also standing as a testament to the persistence of those that society deems undesirable: "No matter how much society tries to extinguish us, we're still here." The Earwurms Conceptual punk band The Earwurms wiggle their way into your ears with savory words and a shebang of sound. Born within the Montessori Lyceum of Amsterdam, they made their way into the Dutch DIY and activist stages, while over the years their identity expanded beyond music to encompass stage outfits and various visual elements. Drawing from no wave, riot girrrl, punk, math rock and art rock, their music explores the joy and understanding found in the banal. ZANJEER زنجیر Hardcore punk band ZANJEER (زنجیر, Urdu for "chain") channels the fury of global injustice through fast, uncompromising hardcore, crust and d-beat sung in Urdu. Vocalist Dozakhi was a prominent figure of Lahore's DIY underground, spending years organizing shows in basements and improvised spaces and fronting bands in a scene with few venues, before relocating to Germany in 2019 in search of an alternative to the religious fundamentalism, patriarchal norms, and sparse scene back home. In recent years, the band sharpened its attack confronting the genocide in Gaza head-on and the everyday racism and Islamophobia in Europe, fusing raw hardcore touchstones with rhythmic ideas from SWANA music traditions. Sarsour صرصور Fast and angry hardcore punk band from Syria and Palestine. Founded this year in Bristol, Sarsour صرصور bring their Arabic anthems and abrasive sounds to totally wired.
title: "TOTALLY WIRED" LE GUESS WHO x ANTIPODE, OCCII, GIRLS TO THE FRONT, ZALZALA

description: Geregeld Ontregeld presents: Die Verlierer, Die Knöpfke & Cavegirl for a night of garage-punk DIE VERLIERER Since their debut in 2022, Die Verlierer have quickly established themselves as one of the most exciting acts in German-language post-punk. Their first album was named one of the year’s best punk records by Maximum Rocknroll, while Notausgang made Bandcamp’s Best Punk Releases of 2024. Legendary sold-out shows at Berlin’s SO36, extensive touring across Germany and Europe, shows in the UK and Mexico have earned Die Verlierer a strong following both at home and abroad. Live, Die Verlierer generate an energy that connects with all kinds of audiences — at festivals and punk clubs just as much as on much heavier line-ups. Their guitar-driven sound is instantly recognisable yet timeless, even as the songs explore a wide range of dynamics and moods. The band have always been political. On their third album, Ideale, their lyrics address war, greed and power more explicitly than ever, reflecting a present in which these issues feel increasingly impossible to ignore. The lyrics confront this reality head-on, while the music offers something in return: freedom, energy and movement. Mixing punk, NDW and new wave, they flirt with both soft and hard sounds, creating their very own sound: "pillow punk". description: Welcome back! HACKEDEPICIOTTO (Alexander Hacke & Danielle de Picciotto) + GLICE (Melle Kromhout & Ruben Braeken) HACKEDEPICCIOTTO (DE) Alexander Hacke (Einstürzende Neubauten) & Danielle De Picciotto (Love Parade, Crime & The City Solution) Both are legends within the underground of the music world. This will be the couple’s first visit to Amsterdam since the last one in 2022. HACKEDEPICIOTTO are Alexander Hacke and Danielle de Picciotto. Both are legends of their own making: Danielle de Picciotto moved to Berlin in 1987, to become the lead singer of the band „Space Cowboys“, the co-initiator of the Love Parade, a collaborator of the Ocean Club with Gudrun Gut, and Alexander’s partner in crime. Alexander Hacke is founding member and bass player of Einstürzende Neubauten. The artist couple, romantically married in 2006, has creatively interacted with countless international projects for almost 2 decades now besides regularly releasing their own compositions. Their live shows are, to put it mildly, intense. Danielle specializes in unusual instruments such as the Hurdy Gurdy, the auto harp and the cemence besides playing the violin and piano; Alexander is master of the bass, guitar and drums. Together they create beautiful, existentialistic, acoustic soundscapes, which roar and vibrate simultaneously leaving their audiences shaken but overjoyed. Danielle, author of two books, writes most of their lyrics, be it the poetic spoken word moments or the momentous choirs they compose together. Alexander Hacke, an excellent throat singer and vocalist, growls his grnarly, rumbling cries that float eerily over their nomadic desert drones, with screeching birds, bees or wild wind accompanying slow, heavy riffs that start as a whisper and end in a volcanic, rolling wave of apocalyptic frenzy. The collage of this mixed with melancholic, translucent harmonies, very heavy & low bass chords, and electronics are a mesmerizing universe of sound and emotion which has generated an ever growing group of enthusiastic listeners. https://hackedepicciotto.bandcamp.com/ Glice is an Amsterdam-based noise duo that has been producing uncompromising, layered electronics since 2015. Using analog equipment and a keen ear for detail, Ruben Braeken and Melle Kromhout craft a sound that moves between hushed musique concrète and industrial noise, between abstract sonic experiments and moments of fragile melody—sometimes dark and ominous, at other times deceptively meditative. Following their critically acclaimed debut LIX (2015), Glice performed at festivals such as Rewire, Incubate and Unsound and released several cassette tapes. Braeken and Kromhout then travelled to Berlin to record the album CIELO (2017) with Alexander Hacke (Einstürzende Neubauten)—a next step in their sonic evolution, where post-industrial textures meet melodic development. This direction continued on the monumental double album PYRE (2021), co-produced by Lasse Marhaug. Exactly ten years after their debut, Glice returns in 2025 with ENVOI. Recorded during a series of concerts with Hackedepicciotto in 2022, this is the purest representation yet of their intense, disorienting live shows: four pieces that build tension layer by layer with distorted voices, piercing noise, rattling synths, fragments of melody, and deep drones. https://glice.bandcamp.com/ Presale/door prices adjusted: our events are set up by volunteers in favour of supporting DIY touring acts, but it is getting ever more risky to plan and book events – please support the community and buy your tickets early! description: MAKING MUSIC IN TIMES OF AUTHORITARIANISM. FILM & TALK WITH MISSISSIPPI RECORDS FOUNDER, ERIC ISAACSON + BHAJAN BHOY (Solo Set) MISSISSIPPI RECORDS PRESENTS : A PEOPLE'S HISTORY OF MUSIC (during times of authoritarianism) A visual and sonic presentation by Eric Isaacson (Mississippi Records) A slideshow / lecture / film presentation from Mississippi Records founder Eric Isaacson telling a story of global music scenes that struggled and endeavoured during periods of authoritarianism. This is a timely and compelling interweaving of people and places, of past and present, of making and sharing music in very troubling times. It's the story of how the powerful interests try to control music and how people fight back, nimbly evading systemic repressions by puritans, corporations and tech lords alike. Making wide, bold swings, this show, covers music from Ethiopia, North Korea,Kenya, the USA and beyond, while drawing on Eric’s colorfully described, personal experiences of the fascist creep. [video width="288" height="360" mp4="https://occii.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/TRAILER-FINAL-MOBILE-VERSION.mp4"][/video] Eric is known for his humbly comical, singular style and for his ability to revitalize audiences through digging up buried treasures from the global music underground. He has an intuitive and captivating way of finding the kinks, idiosyncrasies and soulful stories in the histories of under-acknowledged punk, gospel, soul, blues and roots based music from around the world. Eric has previously constructed and internationally toured three other mind-altering presentations, but never one as timely as this — a must-experience sampling of audio and visual folk art. This whirlwind presentation of archival film, sound clips and images avoids political grandstanding, instead emphasizing vital anti-authoritarian stories of resistance through samizdat music distribution. Eric Isaacson is the founder of Mississippi Records and many other small esoteric record labels such as Cairo, Pyramid and Velvet Ramp. Over the past twenty- three years he's released over 390 records and 165 mixtapes of DIY music from around the world. This catalog includes punk, African guitar griots, Greek criminal underground music, deep country blues, Gospel, Folk, Estonian classical music, Soul, Spiritual Jazz and much more. Eric conceptualized, designed the covers, edited, worked with artists and their ancestors, wrote the liner notes, assembled and mailed these records out. For its first seventeen years Mississippi Records operated with zero internet presence, released no digital music and ran a cash only record store in Portland, Oregon. The company refused all press inquiries and never appeared on social media. Even with these limitations, Mississippi managed to sell over one million records. Beyond releasing records and running a retail shop, Eric has traveled with presentations like this for the past twelve years. These performances all champion DIY culture and try to expose the exploitative nature of the mainstream music industry. description: NEPTUNE (US) + POLARIZED NEPTUNE (US) https://www.neptune-band.com/ After twelve years of relative quiet, experimental rock band Neptune returns with Play Some Music, their ninth full length album and a return to form from a project spanning over three decades. Play Some Music reunites the band’s most recognizable and widest travelling line-up of Jason Sidney Sanford, Mark William Pearson, and Daniel Paul Boucher, whose 2008 LP Gong Lake (Table of the Elements) and 2006 LP Patterns (Les Potagers Natures) serve as defining releases among the band’s catalogue of over thirty recordings. Wielding their distinctive homemade instruments - a melding of hardware store and landfill – Play Some Music features microtonal and macrotonal wire-framed steel guitars as well as amplified drums, amplified circular saw blade percussion, electronics, and feedback organ to produce a suite of songs, improvised and composed, that explore classical mythology and the nebulous realm of memory. Always expanding their sound world, Neptune’s signature frenetic guitars and drums are joined by new gamelan-like amplified percussion and phantasmagoric electronic textures hovering over its ether. Neptune "Play Some Music" by Sleeping Giant Glossolalia Released by esteemed outré music label Sleeping Giant Glossolalia, home to artists such as Ramleh, Ava Mendoza, and Multicult, Play Some Music was recorded by Jason LaFarge at Seizure’s Palace Recording (Swans, Sightings, Akron/Family) and mastered by James Plotkin (Sunn O))), Tim Hecker, Pauline Oliveros). Its gatefold artwork features paintings by Sean Micka from his series Book Out Of Stock But Six Pictures, a meditation on the little-known Nazi resistance fighter Mildred Fish Harnack. Though largely active in Boston since its founding in 1994, the band members currently reside in Boulder, CO; Tucson, AZ; and Durham, NC. The band will support with their lengthiest US tour since 2008 with European dates to follow. description: Hit Like a Girl (US) Announcing their Burning At Both Ends tour, Queer heartache is a unique experience, and one that Hit Like a Girl knows well. Drawing influence from pop, emo, indie and even hardcore, the band channels yearning, love and loss into intimate yet catchy music that may resonate with fans of Tigers Jaw, Future Teens, or Indigo De Souza. Hit Like a Girl is the songwriting project of Nicolle Maroulis (they/them), joined by a rotating live line-up that now features Mol White (they/them) on synth and backing vocals, Mike Davis (he/they) on drums and backing tracks, and rotating members on guitar. Hit Like a Girl strives to represent trans and queer artists, and inspire them to follow their creative pursuits. In 2016 Maroulis founded No More Dysphoria, a 501(c)3 non-profit organization created with the goal of helping transgender individuals pay for major aspects of their transition. Maroulis is a masterful and prolific songwriter. In the eight years since Hit Like a Girl’s inception in 2017, Maroulis has released 4 full length records (You Make Sense (2017), What Makes Love Last (2018), Heart Racer (2021)) and one EP (Becoming (2022)). The band has performed alongside the likes of Mom Jeans, Kississippi, Origami Angel, Pool Kids, and Prince Daddy and the Hyena, and has toured with acts including John-Allison Weiss and The Iron Roses.
